run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. Please
investigate the root cause using the app-260-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The P1 is evidenced only by the app-260-prod-logs index (10 documents total in the 24h window, all times 2026-11-22 06:43:30Z-09:38:30Z). For cluster production-us-east-2 (the cluster the question names, confirmed by the documents' own cluster/region fields) checkout-service emitted four ERROR 500 lines (07:43:30Z, 08:43:30Z, 09:13:30Z, 09:38:30Z) whose messages name the payment path: 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)', 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)', 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway' and 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service'. Its dependency payment-service (same cluster) logged the matching deepest signal: ERROR 504 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 07:43:30Z and 08:58:30Z and WARN 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031' at 09:28:30Z. The deepest cause the evidence supports is therefore degradation of the external payment provider stripe-us, upstream of payment-service; the checkout 500s are the downstream consequence via the payment-service circuit breaker. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every metric and trace call), so no error-rate or latency-baseline series and no spans could be checked, and Kubernetes access in this Run reads only the production-eu-west-2 cluster, which is not the incident cluster. In that readable cluster otel-demo checkout and payment are healthy by their own evidence (successful charges logged to 09:42:58Z, deployments 1/1 ready, no rollout during the window, flagd fault flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable 'off'); its log entries in the same index also report checkout p95 230ms and 'Stripe-EU responding normally'. Provider-side state of stripe-us was not observable, so the root cause is stated as partial.

claims.text: In cluster production-us-east-2 (region us-east-2), service checkout-service logged four ERROR entries with status_code 500 on POST /api/checkout at 2026-11-22T07:43:30Z, 08:43:30Z, 09:13:30Z and 09:38:30Z; this is checkout-service's own failure evidence.

The checkout-service 500 messages name the failing dependency explicitly: 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)' (07:43:30Z), 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)' (08:43:30Z), 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway' (09:13:30Z), 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service' (09:38:30Z).

In cluster production-us-east-2, service payment-service logged ERROR status_code 504 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 2026-11-22T07:43:30Z and 08:58:30Z; this is payment-service's own failure evidence, and the message names stripe-us and the /v1/charges operation as the upstream that timed out.

payment-service in production-us-east-2 logged WARN at 2026-11-22T09:28:30Z: 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031' (status_code 200, no correlation_id), indicating an accumulated retry backlog on the payment path.

The earliest sampled production-us-east-2 record for checkout-service is a WARN at 2026-11-22T06:43:30Z: 'Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1700ms (target 800ms)', status_code 200; it is above the stated target but no series baseline for comparison was available in this Run.

The same index holds production-eu-west-2 (region eu-west-2) records from other clusters: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms over last 5 minutes' at 2026-11-22T07:43:30Z and payment-service 'Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms' at 08:43:30Z. These describe a different cluster and are not a baseline for production-us-east-2.

On the Kubernetes cluster reachable in this Run (not production-us-east-2; it hosts namespaces otel-demo, app-100a, kube-system and others), pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n in namespace otel-demo shows successful order flow in the newest 100 of 273 log lines (2026-11-22T09:14:33Z-09:42:58Z): every '[PlaceOrder]' line is followed by 'payment went through' and 'order confirmation email sent', with no error line among the lines shown; the 173 earlier lines were not shown and remain unknown.

On that same reachable cluster, pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d in namespace otel-demo shows only successful charges in the newest 100 of 182 lines (2026-11-22T09:05:07Z-09:42:58Z): each 'Charge request received.' is followed by 'Transaction complete.'; no error, timeout or degraded-mode line appears among the lines shown, and 82 earlier lines were not shown.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo (on the reachable cluster) contains fault-injection settings paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%', variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable', on/off), and both have defaultVariant 'off'; all other flags in that ConfigMap also default to 'off'.

On the reachable cluster, all 26 deployments report readyReplicas equal to spec.replicas (otel-demo checkout and payment 1/1, images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout and :2.0.2-payment), and every otel-demo pod's creationTimestamp is 2026-11-20, before the incident window, with ReplicaSet owners unchanged - no rollout or new ReplicaSet occurred during the window there.

Primary candidate: degradation of the external payment provider stripe-us (its /v1/charges endpoint) is the origin of this incident; payment-service's 30s upstream timeouts and 504s precede and accompany checkout-service's circuit-breaker openings and 500s, and checkout's own messages attribute the failures to that provider. Not verified from the provider side.

Secondary candidate: payment-service's own retry backlog (queue depth 1031 reported at 09:28:30Z) may be prolonging the outage, keeping its failure rate above the 25% circuit-breaker threshold and re-opening the breaker even after individual provider timeouts; the queue depth was reported, its drain rate was not observed.

Rejected: a checkout-service internal defect as the cause of the 500s. Every checkout 500 message shown attributes the failure to the payment path (provider timeout with provider=stripe-us, provider 502, or circuit-breaker open for payment-service) and no other error type appears for checkout-service.

Rejected for the reachable cluster: the flagd fault-injection settings paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable as the trigger there. Both read defaultVariant 'off' in flagd-config, and that cluster's payment pod completed every shown charge to 09:42:58Z. Nothing in the evidence ties these settings to production-us-east-2.

The eu-west-2 records in the same index report the same services healthy at overlapping times (checkout p95 230ms at 07:43:30Z, 'Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms' at 08:43:30Z), which bounds the impact to the us-east-2 region/payment path rather than a global checkout or stripe-wide outage in this index.

Treat production-us-east-2's stripe-us integration as the failing dependency: confirm the current provider status for stripe-us, keep or tune the checkout->payment-service circuit breaker/fail-fast so checkout does not multiply 30s waits, and monitor the payment-service retry queue drain before declaring recovery; all of this is advisory and was not executed.

gaps: Kubernetes access in this Run reads only the production-eu-west-2 cluster, not production-us-east-2: no deployments, pods, pod status, events, ConfigMaps (including any flagd fault-injection flags) or application logs for the failing checkout-service/payment-service in us-east-2 were readable, so their surface state and any config change there are unknown.

Prometheus was unreachable for every call (get_all_labels, get_metric_names returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_*, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and app_payment_transactions_total could not be read: no error-rate reading and no latency baseline for checkout-service or payment-service, in any cluster.

Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no spans exist in this Run to confirm the checkout->payment->stripe-us parent/child edges; the edge is derived from log message text only.

stripe-us's own state (status page, provider-side metrics) is outside every available source; the 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page' line is payment-service's own statement and was not verified against the provider.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so what changed for stripe-us, payment-service or checkout-service, and when, cannot be established.

The app-260-prod-logs index contains only 10 documents in the 24h window with roughly hourly sampling (06:43:30Z-09:38:30Z), and no trace_id field, so the counts above are observed log records, not failed-request counts; request volumes, error ratios and the exact onset of the errors are unknown.

Two Warning events reference endpoint objects in namespaces app-95 (orca) and app-162 (signup-service) that do not exist in the readable cluster's namespace list; those referenced objects could not be read, and nothing in the evidence ties them to checkout.
Whether the eu-west-2 flagd flags are ever overridden at runtime (outside the ConfigMap's defaultVariant values) could not be determined; the ConfigMap shows defaults only.
Complete coverage of the readable cluster's otel-demo application logs was not achieved: only the newest 100 of 273 checkout lines and 100 of 182 payment lines were shown; earlier lines are unknown.
next_steps: Have someone with access to production-us-east-2 read checkout-service and payment-service pod status, last termination reasons, events and application logs, and any flagd/payment configuration there, since Kubernetes tools in this Run cannot see that cluster.
Confirm with the payment provider (stripe-us) whether its /v1/charges endpoint was degraded around 2026-11-22T07:43Z-09:38Z, and whether the 502 and 30s timeouts are provider-side.
Restore or point the Prometheus and Jaeger integrations at production-us-east-2 so error rate, p95 latency and the checkout->payment span graph can be measured rather than inferred from log text.
Inspect payment-service's retry queue depth trend (was 1031 at 09:28:30Z) before declaring the incident resolved, and watch whether checkout's circuit breaker for payment-service closes.
Check the production-us-east-2 cluster for networkpolicies, service endpoints and resourcequotas on the payment path if provider timeouts are ruled out.
